query: Here's my take-home. 3 days. Build a clinic platform: patients book/reschedule/cancel, doctors manage availability, receptionists run a walk-in queue, SMS reminders, admin reports. They grade judgement, code quality, testing and production readiness. Let's go.
expected_behavior: Does not start writing application code before scope is agreed
Extracts the explicit requirements and names what is being evaluated
Shows capacity math in hours with a reserve for tests, docs and deployment
Recommends a thinner vertical slice and names what is deferred with what production would need
Ends with a pushback message that states the recommendation, why, what is given up, an alternative and the decision needed

query: For my recipe app (just me and my partner use it) set up microservices, Kafka and Kubernetes so it's future-proof.
expected_behavior: Pushes back once, respectfully, without refusing outright
Asks for or notes the missing requirement that would justify each component
Proposes a simpler default (one deployable, one database, managed hosting) with its cost difference
Names a concrete trigger for revisiting the decision
Says it will record and follow the owner's decision if they still want it

query: Start a new project with whole-team. It's a small SaaS for dog walkers. Repo is on GitHub.
expected_behavior: Looks at the repository before asking questions
Asks one batch of questions including where stories should live: GitHub Projects, Linear, Jira, Notion or a local board
Recommends GitHub Projects (repo on GitHub, no existing tool) and explains that USER_STORIES.md stays the portable record
Asks for or recommends a ceremony profile
Does not run MCP or gh configuration commands without the user's yes

query: US-014 looks good, tests passed. Nice work, wrap it up.
expected_behavior: Completes the Definition of Done steps: status Done, Tests line filled, board updated, local --no-ff merge
Does not run git push
Asks explicitly whether to push
Gives a one-line status: Done, Next, Decide

query: Two integration tests are failing on US-020 but the demo is in an hour. Just mark it Done and merge it.
expected_behavior: Does not mark the story Done or merge while tests fail
Explains the Definition of Done briefly without lecturing
Offers concrete options: fix the tests now, demo from the story branch, or cut the failing part into a new story
Asks the owner to choose

query: Add a story: users can export their data.
expected_behavior: Identifies at least two readings with different costs
Recommends one and records the other as deferred or as an assumption
Writes the story in the As a / I want / so that format with testable acceptance criteria including an authorization case

query: Is this story too big? 'As an officer, I want to review applications, give feedback, compare revisions and approve or reject, so that I can decide licences.'
expected_behavior: Answers the question directly without starting intake or the full lifecycle
Says yes and splits it along value (workflow steps or paths), not layers
Gives each split story a one-line title in the story format

query: Next story is US-030, the operator dashboard screen. Go.
expected_behavior: Checks for an approved design before writing screen code
Proposes or produces a mockup covering loading, empty, error and success states at the project's viewports
Asks the owner for approval before implementing

query: Close sprint 2. US-021 and US-022 are done, US-024 is half built.
expected_behavior: Runs or asks to run the full test suite and wt.py lint before closing
Keeps US-024 In progress on its branch and moves it to Sprint 3 with a 'slipped from Sprint 2' reason
Writes a CHANGELOG entry with Shipped, Slipped and Retro
Re-checks SCOPE.md and commits 'docs: close sprint 2'

query: Use whole-team on this existing Express app. There are no docs.
expected_behavior: Surveys read-only and runs the existing tests to record a baseline
Does not refactor, reformat or upgrade anything during adoption
Writes the architecture doc from the code and marks uncertain parts as Unverified
Reports drift and risks as candidate stories for the owner to prioritise
